meds: amlodipine, valsartan, lisinopril, metoprolol, tiotropium, salbutamol PRN, paracetamol PRN, tamsulosin, apixaban
notes: PSA 6 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.08. Prostate volume 79 mL. csPCa 0.77.

note_sections.t: Follow-up consultation to discuss management options following recent biopsy confirmation of Gleason 4+3 prostate adenocarcinoma.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management in a seventy-seven-year-old retired primary school teacher. The patient has a significant medical history including hypertension, atrial fibrillation on apixaban, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease managed with tiotropium and salbutamol, and osteoarthritis. He lives with his wife and remains physically active, completing a daily forty-five-minute walk, while consuming minimal alcohol. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS of 7, currently controlled on tamsulosin, and recently completed a routine surveillance colonoscopy without complications. Given his anxiety regarding invasive procedures, he has requested a thorough discussion of all available therapeutic pathways.

On digital rectal examination, the prostate is enlarged but smooth and symmetrically non-nodular, correlating with a clinical T1c staging. General inspection reveals a well-nourished gentleman with stable vital signs and clear lung fields on auscultation despite his known pulmonary history. Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no palpable lymphadenopathy or organomegaly.
